params.sideJobRate: = otMultiplier x regular rate (W-2, not overtime)

quantities.name: ahe_latest
quantities.meaning: Last observation in data/AHETPI.csv: national AVERAGE hourly earnings of production and nonsupervisory employees, total private, seasonally adjusted, for the single month June 2026 (not a median, not an annual figure).

quantities.name: ahe_date
quantities.meaning: Observation month of ahe_latest (2026-06-01, rendered "June 2026"); the data's "current" date.

quantities.name: regular_rate_usd
quantities.meaning: ahe_latest rounded to whole dollars; the regular hourly rate of the single modeled worker only.

quantities.name: ot_rate_usd
quantities.meaning: 1.5 x regular_rate_usd for the modeled worker; also the hourly pay assumed for that worker's second job.

quantities.name: extra_pay_usd
quantities.meaning: Gross pay for the modeled worker's 400 extra hours in tax year 2026 at ot_rate_usd; identical on both paths.

quantities.name: ot_premium_deduction_usd
quantities.meaning: Half-time premium on the modeled worker's 400 overtime hours in 2026 (0.5 x regular_rate_usd x 400), deductible from federal income tax; overtime path only.

quantities.name: deductible_share_of_ot_pay_pct
quantities.meaning: ot_premium_deduction_usd as a share of extra_pay_usd for the modeled worker (equals 1/3 for any rate at 1.5x), 2 decimals.

quantities.name: ot_income_tax_on_extra_usd
quantities.meaning: Added 2026 federal income tax caused by the 400 extra hours on the OVERTIME path for the modeled worker ($32 regular rate, single, 2026 rules, 400 extra hours).

quantities.name: side_income_tax_on_extra_usd
quantities.meaning: Added 2026 federal income tax caused by the 400 extra hours on the SECOND-JOB path for the modeled worker ($32 regular rate, single, 2026 rules, 400 extra hours).

quantities.name: payroll_tax_on_extra_usd
quantities.meaning: Employee social security + medicare (7.65%) on extra_pay_usd for the modeled worker in 2026; same on both paths.

quantities.name: ot_extra_take_home_usd
quantities.meaning: 2026 take-home from the 400 extra hours on the OVERTIME path for the modeled worker ($32 regular rate, single, 2026 rules, 400 extra hours).

quantities.name: side_extra_take_home_usd
quantities.meaning: 2026 take-home from the 400 extra hours on the SECOND-JOB path for the modeled worker ($32 regular rate, single, 2026 rules, 400 extra hours).

quantities.name: ot_advantage_usd
quantities.meaning: Overtime take-home minus second-job take-home for the modeled worker ($32 regular rate, single, 2026 rules, 400 extra hours), per year.

quantities.name: ot_total_tax_rate_on_extra_pct
quantities.meaning: Federal income + payroll tax as % of the extra pay, OVERTIME path, modeled worker only, 2 decimals.

quantities.name: side_total_tax_rate_on_extra_pct
quantities.meaning: Federal income + payroll tax as % of the extra pay, SECOND-JOB path, modeled worker only, 2 decimals.

quantities.name: side_breakeven_rate_usd
quantities.meaning: Second-job hourly rate giving the modeled worker the same 2026 take-home on 400 hours as overtime at ot_rate_usd; this example only, 2 decimals.

quantities.name: premium_per_hour_usd
quantities.meaning: Deductible premium in each overtime hour of the modeled worker (0.5 x regular_rate_usd = $16 of each $48 hour).

quantities.name: marginal_bracket_pct
quantities.meaning: Single 2026 bracket rate that applies to ALL of the modeled worker's extra taxable pay on both paths (computed; None if the extra pay straddles a bracket).

quantities.name: breakeven_markup_usd
quantities.meaning: side_breakeven_rate_usd minus ot_rate_usd for the modeled worker only ($32 regular rate); scales with the regular rate, not a general constant.

quantities.name: ot_advantage_per_hour_usd
quantities.meaning: ot_advantage_usd / 400 for the modeled worker (= premium_per_hour_usd x marginal_bracket_pct).

quantities.name: breakeven_markup_share_of_ot_rate_pct
quantities.meaning: 100 x breakeven_markup_usd / ot_rate_usd for the modeled worker (10.42); at the 22% bracket with a 1.5x overtime rate it equals 100 x 0.5 x 22% / (1 - 7.65% - 22%) / 1.5 for any regular rate whose extra and break-even pay stay in that bracket, so it supports "about a tenth" as the general rule (ERRATA E1).

quantities.name: EXTRA_HOURS_PER_WEEK
quantities.meaning: Extra hours a week in the viewer scenario (viewer identity number).
quantities.cite: viewer scenario, card.json viewer; result.json assumptions[1]

quantities.name: EXTRA_WEEKS
quantities.meaning: Weeks a year the extra hours are worked.

quantities.name: EXTRA_HOURS_YEAR
quantities.meaning: EXTRA_HOURS_PER_WEEK x EXTRA_WEEKS: extra hours a year, both paths.

quantities.name: REGULAR_HOURS_PER_WEEK
quantities.meaning: Regular weekly hours; also the FLSA threshold above which overtime is required.

quantities.name: REGULAR_WEEKS
quantities.meaning: Weeks a year of regular work (base wages = rate x 40 x 52).

quantities.name: OT_MULTIPLIER
quantities.meaning: Overtime pay multiple of the regular rate.

quantities.name: PREMIUM_MULTIPLIER
quantities.meaning: Part of each overtime hour above the regular rate (qualified overtime compensation).
quantities.cite: 26 U.S.C. 225(c)(1) (only the amount in excess of the regular rate)

quantities.name: OT_CAP_SINGLE_USD
quantities.meaning: Annual cap on the overtime deduction, single filer.

quantities.name: OT_PHASE_START_MAGI_USD
quantities.meaning: MAGI above which the overtime deduction phases down, single filer.

quantities.name: STD_DEDUCTION_SINGLE_USD
quantities.meaning: 2026 standard deduction, single.

quantities.name: BRACKET_RATE_12_PCT
quantities.meaning: 2026 single bracket rate on taxable income $12,400-$50,400.

quantities.name: BRACKET_RATE_22_PCT
quantities.meaning: 2026 single bracket rate on taxable income $50,400-$105,700.

quantities.name: EMPLOYEE_PAYROLL_PCT
quantities.meaning: Employee payroll tax rate on wages (6.2% social security + 1.45% medicare; wage base not reached); = model constant FICA / params.employeePayrollRate.
quantities.cite: 26 U.S.C. 3101(a) (6.2% employee social security tax); 26 U.S.C. 3101(b)(1) (1.45% employee medicare tax)

quantities.name: TAX_YEAR
quantities.meaning: Tax year modeled.

quantities.name: OT_DEDUCTION_FIRST_YEAR
quantities.meaning: First tax year of the overtime deduction (year; V6a exemption).
quantities.cite: not quoted in sources.json provisions (OBBBA effective date); advisory

quantities.name: OT_DEDUCTION_LAST_YEAR
quantities.meaning: Last tax year of the overtime deduction under current law.

data.role: regular hourly rate = last non-missing value rounded to whole dollars; lastObservation 2026-06-01

ruleConstants.name: brackets (single 2026)
ruleConstants.cite: IRS IR-2025-103 (2026 single brackets); IRS IR-2025-103 (2026 top bracket)

ruleConstants.name: qualified overtime = premium over regular rate
ruleConstants.cite: 26 U.S.C. 225(c)(1) (only the amount in excess of the regular rate)

ruleConstants.name: employeePayrollRate
ruleConstants.cite: 26 U.S.C. 3101(a) (6.2% employee social security tax); 26 U.S.C. 3101(b)(1) (1.45% employee medicare tax)

newKindNeeds.computation: Regular rate W = round(last AHETPI value); base wages B = W x 40 x 52; extra pay E = 1.5W x 400 on both paths; premium P = 0.5W x 400. Federal income tax T(x) on the single 2026 schedule; incremental income tax on the extra = T(B + E - 16,100 - D) - T(B - 16,100) with D = min(P, 12,500) on the overtime path (MAGI < 150,000 asserted, so no phase-down) and D = 0 on the second-job path; payroll tax = 7.65% x E on both paths; take-home = E - payroll - incremental income tax; advantage = overtime take-home - second-job take-home; total tax rate = 100 x (1 - take-home / E); break-even second-job rate R solves take-home(R x 400, D = 0) = overtime take-home, by bisection on [1.5W, 4.5W].
invariants: extra_pay_usd identical on both paths; payroll_tax_on_extra_usd = 0.0765 x extra_pay_usd on both paths (±$0.005).
deductible_share_of_ot_pay_pct = 33.33 (premium / overtime pay = 0.5/1.5) whenever premium <= cap.
take-home = extra_pay - payroll - income tax on each path (±$0.01).
When all extra taxable pay on both paths lies in one bracket of rate r: ot_advantage_usd = min(premium, cap) x r (±$0.01); here r = 22%, so 1,408 = 6,400 x 0.22.
side_breakeven_rate_usd >= ot_rate_usd, and second-job take-home at the break-even rate equals ot_extra_take_home_usd (±$0.01).
max AGI (second-job path) < otPhaseDownStartMagi, and premium <= otDeductionCap, so the full deduction applies.

ot_total_tax_rate_on_extra_pct < side_total_tax_rate_on_extra_pct; with UNROUNDED rates, (side rate - overtime rate) x extra_pay / 100 = ot_advantage_usd (±$0.01) (the 2-decimal rates give 1,407.36, not 1,408).
